title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a Grothendieck research note. It is the last page (sheet VI) of a student's written work, headed 'CORNU Ph 16/06/78, C4 Math' (a Montpellier licence/maîtrise certificate). It apparently ended up among the Teichmüller notes because Grothendieck reused the paper as scrap; the neighbouring pages are computations on π_{0,3}, SL(2,Z/n) and related groups, presumably written on the other sides of such sheets.

The first paragraph appears to be the student's conclusion about the icosahedron. The 30 edges form 15 pairs of opposite edges. The 15 lines joining midpoints of opposite edges group into 5 mutually orthogonal triples ('trièdres'). The rotation group permutes these 5 triples, which gives the isomorphism with A5. Each triple accounts for 6 edges. Giving each triple a colour colours all 30 edges with 5 colours, 6 edges per colour. The 6 edges of one colour are pairwise vertex-disjoint and cover all 12 vertices. So this is a decomposition of the icosahedral graph into 5 perfect matchings: a 1-factorization, i.e. a proper edge colouring with 5 colours, which is optimal since the graph is 5-regular. The statement is correct.

The second paragraph is the teacher's remark, presumably Grothendieck's, followed by a signature. He says the student should also have discussed the full automorphism group of the icosahedron, whose centre consists of the identity and the antipodal map. Indeed the full isometry group is A5 × {±1} (order 120), with centre {±1}. The rotation subgroup A5 has trivial centre. The words 'neutre' (identity element) and 'antipodisme' (central symmetry x ↦ −x) are the remark's own terms. The struck-out 'ordre' suggests he started to say something about the order. The remark is correct and elementary.

ideas.what: The 5 orthogonal triples of edge-midpoint axes give a 5-colouring of the icosahedron's edges in which each colour class is a perfect matching; the rotation group acts on the 5 triples.
ideas.modern_name: 1-factorization of the icosahedral graph; the 5 inscribed orthogonal frames (or octahedra) realizing A5 ≅ icosahedral rotation group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Vorlesungen über das Ikosaeder, 1884, and earlier)

ideas.what: The full automorphism group of the icosahedron has centre {identity, antipodal map}.
ideas.modern_name: Full icosahedral group I_h ≅ A5 × Z/2, centre {±1}

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a 1978 student's exam/report on the icosahedron with a short, correct, elementary teaching remark by the grader. It was presumably kept because the sheet was reused as scrap for the 1981-83 Teichmüller computations. There is no research content here; the faint link to the A5 and level-structure themes on the neighbouring pages is coincidental.
transcription_corrections: The header 'CORNU Ph 16/06/78 / C4. Math' and the 'VI' mark this as sheet VI of a student's copy, not as Grothendieck notes.
The first paragraph is the student's text; the paragraph beginning 'En relation avec tout ça' and the signature are the grader's comment (presumably Grothendieck).
'il aurait fallu parler ; du groupe' — the semicolon is a stray mark; read 'il aurait fallu parler du groupe des automorphismes de l'icosaèdre'.
The struck-out word at the end is plausibly 'ordre' (deleted), as transcribed.
